title: Hanuman Ansh Ends Historic Run at Rs 341.76 Crore, 2026's Most Profitable Film
excerpt: The Hindi devotional drama, made for an estimated Rs 1.8 crore, closes its 80-day run as Bollywood's most profitable film of 2026 — but misses the Rs 350 crore milestone and finishes below Border 2.
body:
• Hanuman Ansh, a Hindi-language devotional drama released on August 7, has earned Rs 341.76 crore net in India in 80 days and is projected to finish at Rs 343-345 crore, according to Koimoi.
  • Made on an estimated budget of just Rs 1.8 crore, it is Bollywood's most profitable film of 2026, with Koimoi putting its return at 18,886.67% and profit at Rs 339.96 crore.
  • The film will miss the Rs 350 crore milestone and finish fourth among 2026's Hindi grossers, behind Dhurandhar 2, Drishyam 3 and Border 2.
  • Sacnilk puts its worldwide gross at Rs 451.82 crore, including Rs 48.80 crore from overseas markets.

Hanuman Ansh is ending one of the most unusual theatrical runs in Indian box-office history. The Hindi-language devotional drama has collected Rs 341.76 crore net in India after 80 days in cinemas, according to Koimoi, and is projected to close between Rs 343 crore and Rs 345 crore before it leaves screens ahead of Ramayana, which arrives on November 5.

On day 80, its twelfth Sunday, the film earned Rs 25 lakh, up from Rs 19 lakh on day 79, Zoom TV reported. Those are small daily numbers, but they close a run that rewrote expectations for what a film without stars or scale can do.

"Even its eleventh week set a record — Rs 2.26 crore, the biggest eleventh week ever recorded in India, ahead of Dhurandhar 2's Rs 82 lakh."

A Slow Start That Turned Into a Stampede

The shape of the run is the story. Hanuman Ansh earned just Rs 1.08 crore in its first week and Rs 40 lakh in its second, according to Koimoi's week-wise breakdown. Then word of mouth took over: Rs 10.4 crore in week three, Rs 61 crore in week four, a peak of Rs 90.25 crore in week five and Rs 80.25 crore in week six. Even its eleventh week set a record — Rs 2.26 crore, the biggest eleventh week ever recorded in India, ahead of Dhurandhar 2's Rs 82 lakh.

Directed and written by Vishal Chaturvedi, the spiritual drama runs two and a half hours and carries a U certificate, according to Sacnilk. It released in Hindi on August 7, with a Telugu version following on October 9.

The Most Profitable Bollywood Film of 2026

The ranking tables explain why trade watchers kept returning to this film. Koimoi's most-profitable list for 2026 puts Hanuman Ansh first by a wide margin: an estimated budget of Rs 1.8 crore against Rs 341.76 crore in collections, for a profit of Rs 339.96 crore and a return of 18,886.67%. The next film on the list, Dhurandhar 2, returned 427.25% on a Rs 225 crore budget.

In absolute terms, Hanuman Ansh stands fourth among Bollywood's 2026 grossers in India, behind Dhurandhar 2 (Rs 1,186.32 crore), Drishyam 3 (Rs 369.3 crore) and Border 2 (Rs 362.76 crore), according to Koimoi. Sacnilk adds the global picture: Rs 48.80 crore gross overseas, taking the worldwide gross to Rs 451.82 crore — a substantial diaspora contribution for a devotional title with no conventional star draw.

Why It Stops Short of Rs 350 Crore

Two factors ended the climb. Koimoi and Zoom TV both note that the arrival of Drishyam 3 cut into Hanuman Ansh's run, and that the Telugu version did not perform as expected after its October 9 release. With daily collections now in the lakhs and Ramayana taking screens on November 5, the Rs 350 crore mark is out of reach, and the film will also finish below Border 2's Rs 362.76 crore rather than taking third place for the year.

What It Means

For diaspora audiences, the run is a reminder that devotional and family titles can travel on community word of mouth rather than opening-weekend marketing — Rs 48.80 crore of overseas gross came without a star-led promotional tour dominating the conversation. For the industry, a Rs 1.8 crore production out-earning almost every big-budget release of the year on profit terms will keep the low-budget, high-conviction model at the centre of 2027 slate discussions.

Hanuman Ansh is expected to play its final shows in the coming days. Its closing total, projected at Rs 343-345 crore net in India, will still leave it as the defining box-office outlier of 2026.
